title: Dongye
capsule: Dongye (東濊, Eastern Ye) was a chiefdom occupying the eastern coastal plain of the Korean peninsula — covering modern South Hamgyŏng and Kangwon provinces in North Korea and Gangwon Province in South Korea — attested in Chinese sources from at least the third century BCE. Bordered to the west by the Han Chinese Lelang Commandery and to the north by Goguryeo and Okjeo, the Ye people shared language and ethnic origins with Goguryeo; Chinese records note they supplied sandalwood bows to Lelang and had a population of some twenty thousand households. The polity functioned as a vassal of Goguryeo and was fully absorbed by Gwanggaeto the Great's expansionist campaigns in the early fifth century CE, with a southern remnant passing to Silla.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial boundaries are reconstructed almost entirely from brief passages in Chinese dynastic records (Wei Zhi, Hou Han Shu) and archaeological surveys; precise borders with neighbouring polities remain uncertain and contested.
